findings.reason: The cited Gram–Schmidt theorem requires an inner-product space. The proof establishes a positive Gram quadratic form but does not define and verify the integral inner product on the finite polynomial span. Construct it locally from the finite moments and Gram positivity, preserving the no-choice claim.

The proof invokes thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures, whose statement assumes Countable Choice, while this theorem and its axiom-use declaration do not. Use the choice-free uncompleted-product Fubini/Tonelli result for these polynomial integrands, or prove the finite factorization directly.

The statement says the family indexed by any finite Lambda has constant mode psi_0=1, but Lambda need not contain zero. Make the constant-mode claim conditional on 0 being in Lambda; the orthonormality claim can remain for every finite admissible Lambda.

Its proof also invokes the Countable-Choice-dependent completed-product Fubini result despite declaring no choice use. The integrals of K and the weighted Gram entries follow from the tensor orthonormality result and finite sums, so remove that dependency from the argument.

It relies on lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space, which assumes Countable Choice, while declaring no choice use. The finite coefficient integrals need the integral pairing and Cauchy–Schwarz, not L2 completeness; establish only those choice-free facts.

Its no-choice proof relies on the Countable-Choice-assuming L2 Hilbert supplier for Pythagoras. Prove the finite orthogonality and norm identities directly from the integral pairing, without using completeness.

The axiom-use note says Countable Choice is used only to select a summably Cauchy subsequence, but Step 1.2 also selects strongly measurable representatives for a countable sequence of equivalence classes. Include this countable selection in the stated choice use.

The statement permits any finite Lambda in N0^d, but the tensor basis is defined only within the admissible cutoff box. Require Lambda to be a finite subset of that box; the finite-element-rate corollary must be checked against this condition.

The rate uses k without defining it, and the local interpolation supplier requires a fixed reference element with bounded degrees of freedom. State k and those generic interpolation hypotheses explicitly; do not infer Lagrange nodal boundedness, which has an additional Choice assumption.

The affine-diffusion summary omits the bounded affine forcing F(y)=f0+sum_j y_j f_j required by the model and solution theorem. Include it, and state that the Galerkin chaos set lies in the declared admissible cutoff box.
